A B S T R A C T
The mechanical properties and deformation behaviors of a low-carbon low-density steel of Fe35Mn6Al0.1C are
studied under both room temperature (RT) and liquid nitrogen temperature (LNT). It is found that the yield
strength, tensile strength, total elongation are 251 MPa, 580 MPa and 52 % at RT, which increase 497 MPa, 945
MPa and to 75.5 % at LNT. The Charpy V-notch impact energy is 331±4 J at RT, which remains an excellent
value of 254 ± 6 J at LNT, indicating an excellent combination of strength and ductility at LNT. The micro
structural evolutions are examined by EBSD in SEM and TEM, it is shown that the RT tensile deformation is
mainly controlled by the dislocation substructure refinement accompanied by deformation twinning just before
the necking However the LNT deformation is controlled by both dislocation substructure refinement and
deformation twinning with twinning started just after yielding. The multiple strain hardenings are divided into
four stages with strain increasing at LNT, rather than two stages phenomena at RT. Deformation twinning is
found in the specimen after ~28 % tensile strain at RT, whereas it is found in the specimen after ~10 % tensile
deformation at LNT. which is seldom reported in low-density steel in literature. Based on the analysis of the
relation between work hardening behaviors and microstructure evolution, the high stacking fault energy (SFE)
twinning and its orientation dependence are mainly attributed to the stress concentration induced by planar
dislocation substructure. The exceptional combination of strength and toughness at LNT makes the low-carbon
low-density steel of Fe35Mn6Al0.1C to be a promising cryogenic steel.

As it is shown in Fig. 2(b), the work hardening rate in stage A is
sharply decreased with increasing of tensile strain at both RT and LNT.
This sharp decreasing phenomenon could be easily interpreted by the
dislocation accumulation and recovery [30,61]. However, the work
hardening rate at LNT is much higher than that at RT, which could be
attributed to the increased lattice friction stress with decreasing of
deformation temperature as reported found in TWIP steel [30]. This

5. Conclusion
In this research, the low-carbon low-density steel of Fe-35Mn-6Al
0.1C (wt.%) was designed and its microstructure evolution and
mechanical response at both RT and LNT were examined systematically.
Different from the extensively studied low-density steel with a high
carbon content around
massive deformation twinning was found
not only in the tensile deformation mode but in the impact deformation
mode, which gives the combination of excellent strength, ductility and
V-notch impact toughness at both RT and LNT. Based on the study of the
microstructure evolution at both RT and LNT, the factors affecting the
deformation twinning, including SFE, temperature, crystallographic
orientation, Schmid factor, and planar glide were analyzed thoroughly.
The main conclusions can be summarized as follows.
1 In present low-carbon low-density steel, a two-stage deformation
mechanism is observed for RT deformation and four-stage defor-
mation mechanism is revealed for LNT deformation. Its RT behavior
is dominated by dislocation planar slip, cells or cell blocks forming
and refinement, followed with twinning occurring just before the
necking at RT. However, its LNT deformation behavior is found to be
started with the dislocation planar slip firstly, primary twinning
secondly, cells or cell blocks forming and refinement and finally
second deformation twinning at LNT, indicating a strong deforma-
tion twinning dependence on deformation temperature and defor-
mation strain.
2. Regarding to the deformation twinning, the type III grains with
orientation
direction are more inclined to develop
double orientation twins. But few deformed twinning is activated in
type I grains with orientation
and the type II grains with
orientation far from type III and I are more susceptible to the for-
mation of single orientation twins. Regarding to the dislocation
substructure, the type III grains are characterized by a tendency to
form double dislocation glide traces. The type I grains are distin-
guished by the formation of typical dislocation cells. The type II
grains exhibit a preference for the development of single dislocation
glide traces.
3. The working hardening behaviors and strengthening contribution
are strongly affected by the microstructure evolution at both RT and
LNT. Multiple strain hardening mechanisms of the lightweight
cryogenic steel were observed at LNT. It is revealed that an almost
constant hardening rate was obtained in the early stage of defor-
mation due to the primary deformation twinning. Then a continuous
decrease of the hardening rate resulting from the heavily activated
cross slip. For high strain, a constant work hardening is reached
again due to the extensive activation of primary twinning and sec-
ondary twinning, which in turn facilitates multi-stage strain hard-
ening. During deformation at room temperature, dislocation
hardening but not the deformation twinning is the principal
contributor to strain hardening.
